description: GuardRail incident workbench. Move from E2E latency ownership to exact model call, trace, and correlated CPU profile. Provider work is cumulative RPC work; model wait is request wall-clock union.

panels.description: Successful GuardRail end-to-end P95. Use Latency ownership before attributing this to a model or local code.
panels.title: P95

panels.description: Technical errors divided by completed checks. Deny and transform are successful GuardRail outcomes.
panels.title: Errors

panels.description: Request deadline expirations. Model timeouts are broken down below by provider, model, and Action.
panels.title: Timeouts

panels.description: Observed request wall time spent waiting for one or more external model calls. Parallel calls are unioned, never double-counted.
panels.title: Model wait

panels.description: Checks that continued through an explicit fail-open path. Any positive value is a protection incident.
panels.title: Fail-open

panels.description: Global pre-execution rejects on the selected Runner(s). GuardRail and Endpoint filters do not apply because identity is not trusted until authentication and route resolution succeed.
panels.title: Global entry rejects
Latency ownership · Is time spent in model wait, queue, or local work?

panels.description: E2E is user-visible. Model wait is the union of model-call intervals. Provider work is cumulative RPC work and may exceed E2E under parallelism; it is a load/cost signal, not an additive stage. Queue is admission wait.
panels.title: Latency ownership · P95

panels.description: External model RPC P95 grouped by exact Action, provider, model, and operation. Narrow the debug filters before opening traces.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (provider, model, action, le) (rate(guard_runner_model_call_duration_seconds_bucket{guardrail_id=~"$guardrail",endpoint_id=~"$endpoint",runner_id=~"$runner",provider=~"$provider",model=~"$model",action=~"$action"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Model call latency · P95

panels.description: Model RPC throughput by bounded technical result. Timeout, rate-limited, server, transport, and invalid-response failures remain distinct.
panels.title: Model calls/s by result

panels.description: Concurrent external model calls by Runner/provider/model. A rising plateau with rising E2E latency indicates provider or client saturation.
panels.title: Model calls in flight

panels.description: Retry rate and backoff wall time separate provider latency from client-side resilience delay.
panels.title: Retries and backoff
Technical failures · Which stage and dependency failed?

panels.description: Scoped GuardRail request failures by bounded execution stage and reason. This is the primary locator for error and timeout incidents; policy deny/transform outcomes are excluded.
panels.title: Request failures/s by stage and reason

panels.description: Failed external model calls in the selected range. Provider, model, Action, operation, result, and error class identify the failing dependency without inspecting raw request data.

targets.expr: sum by (provider, model, action, operation, result, error_type) (increase(guard_runner_model_calls_total{guardrail_id=~"$guardrail",endpoint_id=~"$endpoint",runner_id=~"$runner",provider=~"$provider",model=~"$model",action=~"$action",result!="success"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Model failures · selected range
Policy behavior · Why did GuardRails allow, deny, or transform?

panels.description: Successful GuardRail throughput split by firewall disposition. Deny and transform are valid policy outcomes, not technical failures.
panels.title: Disposition throughput

panels.description: Unsafe, uncertain, or error findings that caused an intervention, grouped by configured module, risk, immutable policy, recommended Action, and verdict.

targets.expr: sum by (disposition, module_id, risk, policy_id, action, verdict) (increase(guard_runner_guardrail_policy_triggers_total{guardrail_id=~"$guardrail",endpoint_id=~"$endpoint",runner_id=~"$runner",action=~"$action"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Policy triggers · selected range

panels.description: Actions actually applied to content. Compare with policy triggers to distinguish a recommended action from the final enforced intervention.
panels.title: Applied interventions/s
Protection completeness · Which module failed and how did it degrade?

panels.description: Failed or timed-out protection steps by Action, immutable Policy, failure mode, and bounded cause. First stop for incomplete coverage and fail-open incidents.

targets.expr: sum by (module_id, action, policy_id, failure_mode, reason_class) (rate(guard_runner_guardrail_protection_failures_total{guardrail_id=~"$guardrail",endpoint_id=~"$endpoint",runner_id=~"$runner",action=~"$action"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Protection failures/s

panels.description: Incomplete coverage in the selected range, grouped by the concrete failed module or unresolved module identity.

targets.expr: sum by (coverage, module_id, action, policy_id, failure_mode, reason_class) (increase(guard_runner_guardrail_incomplete_coverage_total{guardrail_id=~"$guardrail",endpoint_id=~"$endpoint",runner_id=~"$runner",action=~"$action"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Incomplete coverage · selected range
Global entry path · Before GuardRail and Endpoint identity is trusted

panels.description: Global pre-execution failures on the selected Runner(s). GuardRail and Endpoint filters intentionally do not apply: authentication and route resolution occur before those identities can be trusted. These failures are excluded from GuardRail availability.
panels.title: Global entry failures · authentication, routing, rejection
Trace and profile · Exact slow request to flame graph

panels.description: Sampled GuardRail trace search results. Open a slow trace to inspect guardrail.request and guardrail.model.request spans, provider/model duration, result, retry evidence, and the linked profile action.

targets.query: { resource.service.name = "tasklattice.guard-runner" && name = "guardrail.request" && span.guardrail.id =~ "$guardrail" && span.endpoint.id =~ "$endpoint" && resource.runner.id =~ "$runner" } | select(span.guardrail.id, span.endpoint.id, span.guardrail.result, span.guardrail.disposition, span.guardrail.duration_ms)

panels.title: GuardRail traces

panels.description: Continuous CPU profile. Use when E2E is high but model-wait and queue are low, or open a correlated profile directly from a Tempo span.
panels.title: Runner CPU flame graph

panels.description: Runner request concurrency, admission queue, and external model concurrency.
panels.title: Runner concurrency and queue

panels.description: Zero is healthy. Non-zero signals identify generation lag, a disconnected Runner control stream, or unsynchronized desired state.
panels.title: Control convergence · healthy = 0

panels.description: Global Runner Pool capacity from Controller topology. Compare desired and ready replicas; connected serving Runners confirms the actual fleet membership.
panels.title: Global Runner Pool replicas

panels.description: Age of the last Controller-observed heartbeat for each selected Runner. A rising line separates an offline/stalled Runner from a configuration-only problem.
panels.title: Runner heartbeat age

panels.description: Age across the Runtime Evidence path: local WAL, Controller watermark, Controller outbox, and end-to-end delivery P95. The first rising series identifies where evidence stopped moving.
panels.title: Evidence pipeline age

panels.description: Events waiting locally or in the Controller outbox. A growing local WAL points to export; a growing outbox points to Controller downstream processing.
panels.title: Evidence backlog

panels.description: Bounded Runtime Evidence failures across local WAL writes, Runner export, and Controller ingestion.
panels.title: Evidence failures/s
